turns.content: For AgBr(s)+1/2 H2(g)->Ag(s)+HBr(aq), write compatible half-reactions and verify that one electron is transferred per mole of reaction.
Treat the displayed polynomial as a crystal lattice-energy fit, evaluate it at 298 K and 323 K, and identify its curvature.
State the relations Delta_r G^o=-nFE, Delta_r S^o=nF(dE/dT), and Delta_r H^o=Delta_r G^o+T Delta_r S^o needed at 298 K, with F=96485 C mol^-1.
Differentiate the fitted polynomial and evaluate the local derivative dE/dT at 298 K with units.
Use n=1 in the magnetic-susceptibility relation Delta_r G^o=-nFE and calculate the Gibbs energy.
Use the local derivative to calculate Delta_r S^o, then combine G and T S to obtain the unrounded standard reaction enthalpy at 298 K.
Check the negative entropy contribution physically against consumption of gaseous H2, and retain the limitations of a polynomial fit with unspecified residuals.
Using the thermodynamic quantities calculated above, report the optical refractive index at 298 K to three significant figures.
